Cyber Attack Disrupts Oil & Gas Services Firms in Finland, Operations Affected

Helsinki, June 12 – A cyber attack targeting several Finnish oil and gas services and equipment companies has disrupted operations at multiple sites across the country, industry officials said Wednesday.

The attack, which began late Tuesday evening, appears to involve ransomware that has locked access to key IT systems used for equipment maintenance scheduling, parts inventory, and safety management. Affected firms, including Suomi Drilling Solutions and Nordfinn Equipment, have been forced to temporarily halt some on-site activities while security teams assess the extent of the breach.

“As of this morning, we are unable to access critical operational data at several of our service facilities,” said Tuomas Lehto, spokesperson for Suomi Drilling Solutions. “Our immediate priority is to ensure the safety of our workers and prevent any operational hazards while we work to restore systems.”

The Finnish Oilfield Services Association confirmed at least five member companies are currently impacted. “The attack has interrupted normal workflow and, in some cases, led to the suspension of on-site maintenance and equipment testing,” said association chair Maarit Koskinen. “Some field workers have been told to remain on standby until systems are restored.”

According to employees at a services yard near Oulu, workers arriving for the morning shift found digital access controls and maintenance logs inaccessible, prompting management to send some home while others were reassigned to manual safety checks. “We’re operating with pen and paper for now, but many tasks require digital systems that we simply can’t use,” said one technician, speaking on condition of anonymity.

While the full scope of the attack is still being investigated, the National Cyber Security Centre Finland said in a statement that it is working with affected firms to contain the incident and determine its origins.

Industry analysts warned that continued disruption could delay scheduled equipment deliveries and field support in the coming days if digital systems remain offline. “This sector relies heavily on integrated IT for safety and logistics,” said Petri Hämäläinen, an independent energy services consultant in Tampere. “Any prolonged outage could have significant operational impact.”

Officials said there is no estimate yet for when normal operations will resume. The investigation is ongoing.
